summary.title: A New Organocatalytic Desymmetrization Reaction Enables the Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Madangamine E
summary.authors: Shinya Shiomi; Benjamin D A Shennan; Ken Yamazaki; Ángel L Fuentes De Arriba; Dhananjayan Vasu; Trevor A Hamlin; Darren J Dixon
summary.executive_summary: This paper reports the first enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E, a complex pentacyclic marine alkaloid, in 30 steps. The synthesis is enabled by the development of a novel organocatalytic desymmetrizing intramolecular Michael addition reaction. This key transformation converts a prochiral ketone tethered to a β,β'-disubstituted nitroolefin into a chiral bicyclic core with near-perfect enantio- and diastereoselectivity. The reaction efficiently establishes three stereogenic centers, including a quaternary carbon stereocenter, and is highly scalable. The authors utilized density functional theory (DFT) calculations to probe the mechanism, revealing that the enantio-determining step is an irreversible C-C bond formation stabilized by cooperative hydrogen bonding interactions between the thiourea catalyst, the nitro group, and the enamine intermediate. Following the construction of the rigid bicyclic core, the synthesis proceeded through several key steps, including a mild one-pot oxidative lactamization to form the B ring, a two-step Z-selective olefination of a sterically hindered ketone, and two ring-closing metathesis (RCM) reactions to install the macrocyclic D and E rings. The final product was obtained in good yield and its structure was confirmed by comparison with literature data. This work demonstrates the power of catalytic desymmetrization in generating stereochemical complexity from simple achiral precursors, offering a new strategy for the synthesis of complex natural products.

claims.description: A new organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction enables the enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E.
DFT calculations reveal the origin of enantioselectivity in the catalytic cyclization.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper reports the first enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E, a complex pentacyclic marine alkaloid, in 30 steps. The synthesis is enabled by the development of a novel organocatalytic desymmetrizing intramolecular Michael addition reaction. This key transformation converts a prochiral ketone tethered to a β,β'-disubstituted nitroolefin into a chiral bicyclic core with near-perfect enantio- and diastereoselectivity. The reaction efficiently establishes three stereogenic centers, including a quaternary carbon stereocenter, and is highly scalable. The authors utilized density functional theory (DFT) calculations to probe the mechanism, revealing that the enantio-determining step is an irreversible C-C bond formation stabilized by cooperative hydrogen bonding interactions between the thiourea catalyst, the nitro group, and the enamine intermediate. Following the construction of the rigid bicyclic core, the synthesis proceeded through several key steps, including a mild one-pot oxidative lactamization to form the B ring, a two-step Z-selective olefination of a sterically hindered ketone, and two ring-closing metathesis (RCM) reactions to install the macrocyclic D and E rings. The final product was obtained in good yield and its structure was confirmed by comparison with literature data. This work demonstrates the power of catalytic desymmetrization in generating stereochemical complexity from simple achiral precursors, offering a new strategy for the synthesis of complex natural products.

Research Context
The madangamine natural product family is characterized by an architecturally complex pentacyclic fused-ring system. Previous synthetic efforts have focused on polycyclic core fragments, with only two total syntheses reported. The authors envisioned that an enantioselective desymmetrization reaction could install all stereochemical information. Prior work by the group focused on desymmetrization of α,β-unsaturated esters. Intramolecular desymmetrizing variants establishing quaternary carbon centers were previously unreported.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is whether a catalytic enantioselective desymmetrization can construct the madangamine core. The hypothesis is that a bifunctional primary amine thiourea catalyst can mediate the cyclization. The predicted outcome is the formation of a chiral bicyclic core with high selectivity. The authors hypothesized that the AC bicyclic motif is well-suited for this approach. It was predicted that this strategy would provide a rigid scaffold for further elaboration.

Methodological Details
The study utilized a model substrate, methyl-substituted nitroolefin 7, for catalyst screening. A range of chiral primary and secondary amine organocatalysts were tested. Reactions were conducted in dichloromethane at 20 mol% catalyst loading. Benzoic acid was used as a co-catalyst in the reaction mixture. The final synthesis employed a 30-step sequence to complete madangamine E. A new scalable route to nitroolefin 17 was developed using reductive amination. The butenyl chain was installed via a Michael addition of an organo-zinc-copper complex. Selenoxide elimination was used to install the nitroolefin with E:Z selectivity. The key desymmetrization was performed on a >5g scale. DFT calculations were used to investigate the reaction mechanism.

Procedures And Architectures
The catalytic cycle begins with the formation of a hemiaminal intermediate. Elimination of water forms an imine intermediate, which tautomerizes to an enamine. The key C-C bond forming step is an intramolecular Michael addition. The transition state TS1 is stabilized by hydrogen bonding interactions. The reaction is highly exergonic with a ΔGrxn of -19.4 kcal mol-1. The oxidative lactamization used AZADO, copper chloride, and DMAP. Ring-closing metathesis for the D ring used Grubbs 1st generation catalyst. The macrocyclic E ring was formed using Hoveyda-Grubbs 2nd generation catalyst. A co-catalytic p-benzoquinone was used to minimize isomerization during RCM. The final step involved double amide reduction using excess LiAlH4.

Key Results
Jacobsen's thiourea catalyst 9f provided the bicyclic adduct in 70% yield. The reaction achieved 99% ee and single diastereomer formation. The computed enantioselectivity was 99% ee, matching experimental results. The energy difference between TS1 and the second-lowest TS was 3.0 kcal mol-1. The desymmetrization of nitroolefin 17 yielded product 18 in 95% yield. The reaction on 17 achieved >99% ee and single diastereomer. The RCM to close the D ring gave tetracyclic enone 26 in 82% yield. The RCM to close the E ring gave diamide 30 in 71% yield. The final reduction afforded synthetic madangamine E in 72% yield. The Z-selective olefination achieved 90% Z-selectivity (4.3:1 ratio).

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The enantioselectivity is determined by the irreversible C-C bond formation step. The preferred transition state benefits from cooperative push/pull-type mechanism. The nitro group's lower pKa compared to ester explains the mechanistic difference. The rigid bicyclic core allows for high stereochemical fidelity in subsequent steps. The work demonstrates the utility of desymmetrization for complex scaffold generation.

Contradictions And Limitations
Most tested catalysts gave complex product mixtures rather than cyclized product. The Wittig reaction of ketone 3 was largely unsuccessful due to deprotonation. The organocerium reagent reaction was highly capricious and sensitive to quality. Initial RCM attempts for the E ring failed due to spatial arrangement. The synthesis is long, requiring 30 steps to complete the target.

Claims
A new organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction enables the enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E. The synthesis was completed in 30 steps. The key reaction constructed the chiral bicyclic core. The reaction achieved near-perfect enantio- and diastereoselectivity. The synthesis is lengthy and involves challenging steps. This provides a new method for constructing quaternary carbon centers. It demonstrates the power of catalytic desymmetrization in natural product synthesis.
DFT calculations reveal the origin of enantioselectivity in the catalytic cyclization. TS1 is the most energetically favorable transition structure. The computed ee matches the experimental ee. Hydrogen bonding stabilizes the preferred transition state.  

Data And Code Availability
Detailed synthetic procedures and computational methods are in the Supporting Information.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The reaction was proven highly scalable on a >5g scale. The selenoxide elimination efficiency depended strongly on solvent mixture. The organocerium reaction was sensitive to reagent quality.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the structure of madangamines and the retrosynthetic analysis. Figure 2 illustrates the catalyst screening and DFT mechanism. Figure 3 details the computed reaction pathway and transition states. Figure 4 presents the synthetic route to nitroolefin 17 and the desymmetrization.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a new organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction for quaternary carbon centers. 2. The strongest evidence is the near-perfect selectivity and scalability of the key reaction. 3. The future path involves applying this strategy to other complex natural products.
